newsitem.title: IRELAND: Guarantee Life bought by Irish company for $163 million.
newsitem.headline: Guarantee Life bought by Irish company for $163 million.

text.p: Irish Life Plc said Thursday its U.S. unit Irish Life of North America had agreed to buy the Guarantee Reserve Life Insurance Co. for $163 million.
Irish Life said the acquisition of the privately-owned Illinois-based firm would be funded from its existing resources and from debt financing. The acquisition would enhance earnings, it said.
Managing director David Kingston said in a statement the acquisition represented a significant further development of its U.S. business and would have a major beneficial impact on the group.
He called it "a very successful company in its target market" which would add an innovative distribution channel and open up opportunities for growth at its existing U.S. businesses.
Irish Life said it expected to complete the purchase by April, 1997.

It said the U.S. company was licensed to write life assurance and accidental and health business in 47 states and Washington D.C. It has 175 employees and about 340,000 policyholders. Guarantee Life is based in Calumet City, Ill.
"The company's product and market focus is on providing risk benefits to older age groups," Irish Life said.
